Fresco: business data map

A weekly menu planner for Spanish households whose menus learn from what each Pro household cooks and discards. This map explains the data under it.

Overview

Scope: full-system. Schema source: the migration files in supabase/migrations/ (156 files, oldest 20260725110000_baseline_recipes_catalog.sql, newest 20261029160000_prune_ingredient_seasons.sql), read offline as stack.database.schema_source: migrations in .agents/project.yaml declares. The database itself was not queried for this map; row counts come from supabase/seed.sql and migration headers, each dated where it is stated.

Fresco turns "what do I cook this week?" into a generated weekly menu (7 days by desayuno / comida / cena, up to 21 slots) and an aisle-grouped shopping list. Menus are chosen by deterministic code from a shared recipe catalogue after a SQL food-safety filter (ADR-0005). The differentiator is behavioural learning: every user can mark a slot cocinada or descartada; only a Pro subscriber's next menu reads those marks back (ADR-0001, ADR-0006, ADR-0008, ADR-0063).

Actors

ActorDescription
GuestA visitor on a real Supabase anonymous session (is_anonymous = true, ADR-0003). Generates a full menu with no signup; can convert to an account and keep the same user_id. Abandoned guests are deleted after 3 days.
Free userRegistered, user_profiles.plan = 'free'. Full weekly generation; marks are recorded but never read back into her own menus.
Pro / Family userplan in ('pro','family'), gated in code by isProEntitlementActive (supabase/functions/generate-meal-plan/entitlement.ts). Her recent marks and all-time engagement shape the next menu and a "what we learned" text. Plan state is written only by the Stripe webhook and the reconciliation job.
Waitlist visitorNo account. Leaves an email on the launch waitlist and confirms it by a mailed token (double opt-in).
Owner / operatorWrites the recipe catalogue with the service role (scripts and data migrations), decides seasons, exceptions and the supermarket legal gate, and flips billing_mode at go-live.
Scheduled jobsSix pg_cron jobs inside the database plus GitHub Actions schedules outside it (see automatic-processes).
Stripe (inbound)Calls POST /api/stripe/webhook; the primary writer of subscription state on user_profiles.

How the pieces connect

  • The browser calls Next.js routes (app/api/**: Stripe checkout, portal and webhook, consents, waitlist, guest email, profile export, health and the reconcile cron route) and Supabase Edge Functions (supabase/functions/, nine functions: generate-meal-plan, generate-shopping-list, get-shopping-list-suggestions, update-recipe-status, reassign-guest-data, delete-account, delete-catalog-recipe, retry-posthog-erasures, send-weekly-reengagement-push). It also calls RPCs and reads its own rows directly under RLS.
  • Both the routes and the functions read and write the one shared Supabase Postgres project (jdqemhewjrjuopssdurn, the same for local, dev, staging and production per .agents/project.yaml, ADR-0020). RLS, triggers and pg_cron live there; this is the main data path.
  • Next.js routes call Stripe (checkout, portal, webhook, reconciliation) and send email (subscription confirmation and waitlist token, Gmail SMTP when configured, else Resend).
  • Edge Functions send Web Push (weekly reminder) and events to PostHog; errors go to Sentry from every runtime.

Value

  • Guest / Free: a week of meals and a priced shopping list in seconds, no signup.
  • Pro: menus that avoid what the household discarded and lean on what it cooked, explained in plain language.
  • Owner: food safety, seasons and subscription state are enforced in the database, so a direct write cannot bypass them.

Catalogue size, as of 2026-10-29: public.recipes holds 1287 rows in production, 658 of them active (activo = true). Source: the header of supabase/seed.sql ("verbatim dump of public.recipes from the prod project, 1287 rows, last regenerated 2026-10-29", FRESCO-1064) and a count of the activo value over its 1287 rows. The header of 20261029160000 measured 1167 rows earlier that day; the commit log names 120 recipes inserted by FRESCO-953 in between.

Entities

Every table below is in schema public unless named otherwise. Table creation is cited per row; column lists are in the migrations and lib/supabase/types.ts.

EntityBusiness roleWhy it exists
auth.usersIdentity. is_anonymous separates a guest from a registered account.Every user-owned table hangs off it with ON DELETE CASCADE, so one delete removes a whole footprint (account deletion, guest cleanup). There is no role column: authorisation is row ownership through auth.uid().

Detail: entity-operational-tables.

Key relationships and why

  • auth.users 1:1 user_profiles: the profile is the user's onboarding output; the cascade root is auth.users.
  • user_profiles 1:N meal_plans: one plan per ISO week; the unique key makes regeneration a deliberate delete-then-generate.
  • meal_plans 1:N meal_plan_recipes (up to 21 slots): planning_selection can leave a slot excluida.
  • meal_plans 1:0..1 shopping_lists: the list is built on demand; shopping_lists.user_id is a denormalised column referencing user_profiles, so the guest reassignment moves it explicitly.
  • meal_plan_recipes N:1 recipes: the learning trigger walks this edge to update the recipe's global counters.
  • user_profiles 1:N favorites N:1 recipes: favourites cascade from both sides.
  • recipes 1:N recipe_user_feedback (one row per user and recipe, user_id references auth.users): the first-mark ledger behind the counters.
  • Tables that do not hang off a user: the catalogue tables, the supermarket layer, stripe_webhook_events, billing_mode, account_erasures (hash only, on purpose), job_heartbeat, waitlist_signups and the rate-limit configuration. Deleting a user touches none of them.

Entity: recipes (the catalogue)

The shared catalogue. Shape: nombre, slug, descripcion_corta, meta (raciones, times, dificultad, coste_estimado), clasificacion (cocina, categoria, tipo_plato, es_ligero, es_contundente, ...), dieta (ten boolean flags), alergenos, ingredientes_principales, ingredientes_cantidades, temporada, pasos_resumen, foto_url, the learning counters and activo (column list of the supabase/seed.sql insert).

What is not obvious

  • Soft delete. activo = false retires a recipe without breaking the ON DELETE RESTRICT references from slots (20260908180000, FRESCO-460). As of 2026-10-29: 1287 rows, 658 active, 629 inactive (count over supabase/seed.sql, a dump of production). get_filtered_recipes() and get_catalog() serve active rows only; the table-level read policy does not filter on it.
  • Derived learning counters. veces_cocinada, veces_descartada and ultima_vez_en_menu are written by the trigger recipe_learning_trigger (function update_recipe_learning()), never by a client. Since 20261019200000 they move only the first time a given user cooks or discards a given recipe (recipe_user_feedback). rating_promedio and veces_calificada are no longer written: the rating signal was retired (ADR-0063); the columns stay as history.
  • Computed season. temporada is not typed by hand: it must equal compute_recipe_season(...) on every active row (see entity-recipe-season).
  • Allergen and diet tags under a database barrier. The food-safety filter compares tags only, so a missing tag would serve a recipe to the person who declared that allergy. The trigger recipes_tag_coherence (BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF alergenos, dieta, ingredientes_principales, pasos_resumen, activo) calls recipe_tag_findings() and rejects an active row whose tags contradict its own text with SQLSTATE 23514 (ADR-0064, 20261021094055, 20261021095149). Later migrations widened the rules: wheat products without the word "trigo" (20261022090000) and sin_gluten refused when an ingredient is a brand-dependent wheat carrier such as stock, morcilla, callos or salsa verde (20261023160000, key dieta:sin_gluten_marca). Inactive rows are drafts and save freely. A TypeScript twin in tests/db/recipe-allergen-diet-rules.ts is kept equal by a parity test.
  • Integrity CHECKs. recipes_alergenos_vocab (the 14 EU allergens, 20261013120000), recipes_ingredientes_cantidades_valid (shape, closed unit list, every name present in ingredientes_principales), recipes_ingredientes_principales_distinct, recipes_nombre_sin_con_repetido and recipes_categoria_en_contrato (20261009130000, 20261009140000).
  • Quantities. ingredientes_cantidades (ADR-0042) holds {nombre, cantidad, unidad} for meta.raciones servings. In the 2026-10-29 dump every active row carries it; 566 rows (all inactive) have it null.
  • Who writes. No client role: anon and authenticated can read (policy "Recetas públicas para lectura", 20260729130000); the write policy was dropped (20260726010000). Writes come from the service role (operator scripts, data migrations, delete-catalog-recipe) and the learning trigger.
  • Data-only migrations. Many migrations from 20261008170000 on correct catalogue data by rule (allergens, diets, titles, steps, duplicates, quantities). They change rows, not schema; each carries a guard on the old value so a rerun touches nothing.

Entity: recipe season (computed)

recipes.temporada is a computed value enforced by the database (ADR-0067, extended by ADR-0068, updated 2026-10-29 by FRESCO-1063).

  1. Recipe written. Any insert or update of an active recipe, or a reactivation.
  2. Ingredient rule, compute_recipe_temporada(ingredientes_principales): looks up each ingredient by exact lower-case name in ingredient_seasons. The season is the set of seasons shared by all seasonal ingredients, in calendar order (primavera, verano, otono, invierno).
  3. Shared season: kept as is (gazpacho-like dishes whose ingredients put them in summer stay there).
  4. Conflict (the seasonal ingredients share no season): the function returns NULL and a person decides; any valid value is accepted. Five recipes were pinned this way by 20261027180000; the header of 20261029160000 states that after the prune the 11 recipes then in conflict resolve by themselves.
  5. No seasonal ingredient: the dish rule, compute_recipe_season(ingredientes, slug, clasificacion): first a per-slug row in recipe_season_exceptions; else ['otono','invierno'] when clasificacion.categoria is guiso or sopa, or legumbres and not es_ligero; else ['todo_el_ano'].
  6. Barrier: trigger recipes_temporada_coherence (BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF temporada, ingredientes_principales, activo, slug, clasificacion) calls recipe_temporada_problem(). On every row that carries a season the shape must hold (non-empty, allowed values, no repeats, calendar order, todo_el_ano only alone, recipe_temporada_shape_problem). On an active row the stored season must equal the computed one, else SQLSTATE 23514 naming the recipe, the expected and the stored value. It fires after recipes_tag_coherence (alphabetical order), so an allergen error is reported first.

The tables behind it (as of 2026-10-29)

  • ingredient_seasons holds 14 ingredients: espárragos, espárragos trigueros, ajetes, guisantes, alcachofas, fresas, frutos rojos, melón, kale, berza, grelos, coles de bruselas, membrillo, naranja. Migration 20261029160000 removed 27 rows that are sold all year in a Spanish supermarket (pimiento, espinacas, calabacín, brócoli, berenjena, apio, manzana, pepino, puerro, calabaza, setas, judías verdes, pera and others), the same criterion that kept tomate out from the start. It recomputed the recipes it moved in the same migration.
  • recipe_season_exceptions holds 13 slugs: five from 20261028082818 (the salmorejo to verano; a lentil burger and three miso soups to todo_el_ano) and eight from 20261029160000 (two gazpachos and five cold creams to verano, the falafel to todo_el_ano).
  • Both tables have RLS on, no policy and no grant to anon or authenticated: backend-only data.

Effect and why

The menu selector scores 3 points when a recipe's season includes the planned week's season and 1 point for todo_el_ano (menu-selector.ts), so a season decides how often a recipe is served. The prune's measured impact on active recipes (simulation over the 1167-row catalogue, before the FRESCO-953 insert): summer 126 to 7, spring 63 to 30, autumn 223 to 108, winter 158 to 113, all year 215 to 395. A fixture or generator that writes an active recipe must call compute_recipe_season first or the barrier refuses it.

Entity: user_profiles

  • Ownership. id is the auth.users id; the owner reads and writes her own row under RLS. Deleting the auth user cascades.
  • Subscription columns are server-only. plan, plan_expires_at, stripe_customer_id, stripe_subscription_id, payment_failed_at and, since 20261017161451, stripe_livemode can only change when the writer is the service role: trigger protect_subscription_columns (function prevent_client_subscription_writes(), BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE). RLS is row-scoped, so a policy alone could not stop a user granting herself Pro (ADR-0007).
  • Health data needs consent. Trigger require_health_data_consent refuses a client write that leaves allergies, a dieta_* flag or the free-text diet / allergen fields in the row when the owner has no user_consents row of kind health_data (20261014100000, GDPR art. 9). Clearing is always allowed; the service role is exempt.
  • Allergen vocabulary. alergenos must use the same 14 slugs as recipes_alergenos_vocab (20261019120000): a profile with an unknown spelling would never match a recipe tag and the person would be served the allergen.
  • Bounds. List columns are at most 30 elements and 2400 bytes, name 80 and free text 500 characters, planning_selection an object of at most 4096 bytes (20261013170000); household size has an upper bound (20260902120000).
  • analytics_consent mirrors the cookie-banner choice for signed-in users; server-side analytics send only when it is exactly true (ADR-0044).
  • Removed: sexo and its enum were dropped (20261019160000, data minimisation: nothing read it).

Entity: meal plans and slots

  • Created only by trusted paths. authenticated has no INSERT on meal_plans or meal_plan_recipes (20261002072502). Plans come from create_meal_plan() (service role, one transaction for plan and slots, 20261013160000), copy_meal_plan_to_week() and reassign_guest_data() (SECURITY DEFINER).
  • Week label is real. CHECK meal_plans_semana_iso_valida pins semana_iso to an ISO week; create_meal_plan also checks that fecha_inicio is that week's Monday.
  • Per-user cap. Trigger meal_plans_enforce_quota (BEFORE INSERT, advisory lock) refuses a 105th plan: 104 is two years of weeks (20261019220000).
  • Slot columns are guarded. Trigger protect_mpr_integrity (function protect_meal_plan_recipes_integrity()) refuses a change to estado, rating, recipe_id or sustitucion_ingrediente unless the writer is the service role, an admin session, or a validated RPC that set the app.mpr_trusted_write setting (swap_meal_plan_slots, confirm_ingredient_substitution, assign_recipe_to_slot). Since 20261019120000 client UPDATE is granted column by column; tipo_plato and fecha_inicio are not writable by a client.
  • A null recipe is meaningful. recipe_id is null for an excluida slot and for a slot with no safe recipe (the generator's "no safe recipe" gap, also used by the copy when a recipe no longer passes the filter).
  • Side effects of a slot change: the learning trigger (on estado) and the shopping-list stale trigger (see entity-shopping-lists).

Entity: shopping_lists

  • jsonb on purpose. items is [{nombre (aisle), orden, items: [{nombre, cantidad, unidad, comprado, origen?}]}], at most 100 KB. Edits go through RPCs: jsonb_set_comprado (tick), jsonb_add_item (rejects a non-object element since 20261019120000), jsonb_remove_item (removes only origen: 'sugerencia' items) and jsonb_clear_comprados.
  • Stale flag. desactualizada_desde is set by trigger meal_plan_recipes_mark_shopping_list_stale (function mark_shopping_list_stale()) the first time the plan changes in a way that alters what is bought: a recipe appearing, disappearing or replaced in a slot, a confirmed substitution set or cleared, or a slot entering or leaving descartada / excluida. Marking cocinada does not. generate-shopping-list in refresh mode rebuilds the list in place and clears the flag (20261019190000, FRESCO-1010).
  • Ownership. user_id is a denormalised column referencing user_profiles; INSERT and UPDATE require an owned meal_plan_id.

Entity: user_consents

  • Append-only, server-written. No client role can insert, update or delete. The only writer is record_consents(p_user_id, p_kinds, p_version), SECURITY DEFINER, EXECUTE for the service role only; POST /api/consents takes the user from the session and the version from LEGAL_TEXTS_VERSION (20261019150000). Owners keep SELECT on their own rows.
  • Keyed on auth.users, not user_profiles, so a guest can consent before a profile exists and the rows survive conversion.
  • Once per text version for age_14, terms, privacy, health_data; once per purchase for withdrawal_waiver: a repeat within 30 minutes is a no-op, a later purchase records a new row (20261023121936, FRESCO-1021). At most 100 rows per user.

Entity: supermarket layer

  • supermarket_chain: one row per chain (mercadona, consum, dia, alcampo) with the legal gate permiso, permiso_ref and habilitada (see state-supermarket-chain).
  • supermarket_product (unique (cadena, id_externo), pack size and unit), supermarket_zone (one default zone per chain), supermarket_zone_postcode (empty by design: Fresco stores no postcode), supermarket_price (always the whole-pack price), supermarket_price_history (appended only when price or availability changes) and ingredient_product_match (ingredient key to product, with confianza and confirmado).
  • No user data: global reference data, not touched by account deletion.
  • Reads are gated per chain by private.supermarket_chain_activa(cadena) in RLS and inside get_supermarket_prices; supermarket_chain itself and the history are not readable by authenticated; no client role writes (20261002200000).
  • Whether these tables hold rows today was not verified (see discovery-gaps).

Entity: operational tables

All of these have RLS on, no client policy and no client grant; only the service-role client in the owning route, function or cron touches them.

TableWhat it holdsWhy
stripe_webhook_eventsOne row per handled Stripe event_id: claimed_at, completed_at.Idempotency: Stripe re-delivers (see state-stripe-webhook-events).
billing_modeOne row: the Stripe mode the shared database serves (test until go-live).Every environment shares one database, so a test-mode event from a preview deploy must not make a production account Pro (ADR-0061). Flipped once by the owner; the service role can only read it.
pending_confirmation_emailsIds of subscriptions whose confirmation email was rejected.The confirmation email is a legal duty; the reconcile job retries it under an attempt cap and deletes the row on success (20261017190000).
account_erasuresOne row per erased account: user_hash (SHA-256), Stripe and PostHog outcome, a pending PostHog id only while posthog = 'failed'.The cascade erases every row that could prove an erasure happened; this is the surviving proof and the retry handle. Also used as the queue for guests' PostHog erasure (20261019170000).
job_heartbeatLast successful run per scheduled job.pg_net only enqueues, so the jobs write their own heartbeat and /api/health/jobs reads it.
rate_limits, rate_limit_endpoints, rate_limit_exempt_usersPer-user hourly counters, the registry of allowed endpoints with their ceiling, and an exemption list.check_and_increment_rate_limit accepts only registered endpoints and clamps the limit to the registry (ADR-0010). 13 endpoints are registered (see access-control).
ip_rate_limitsHourly counters keyed by a salted hash of the client address, never the address.Limits the anonymous waitlist route (20261019180000).

Access control

There are no application roles: Postgres roles anon (no session), authenticated (any signed-in session, guests included) and service_role (server code) plus row ownership through auth.uid(). Every public table has RLS enabled; the baseline event trigger rls_auto_enable exists for that purpose. Grants were read from the migrations, not from the live database.

Functions that cross the ownership line

  • SECURITY DEFINER with an actor bind (raise when an identity parameter differs from auth.uid()): get_filtered_recipes, get_catalog, check_and_increment_rate_limit. The Pro history readers get_recent_recipe_marks and get_user_recipe_engagement read only rows where mp.user_id = auth.uid().
  • SECURITY DEFINER, ownership checked inside, one "not found" for missing and foreign rows: swap_meal_plan_slots, copy_meal_plan_to_week (20260928180000).
  • Service role only: create_meal_plan, reassign_guest_data (the one cross-user write), record_consents, the waitlist functions, get_supermarket_demand, get_push_subscriptions_without_current_plan, cleanup_abandoned_guests, recipe_tag_findings and its helpers.
  • SECURITY INVOKER under the caller's RLS: assign_recipe_to_slot, confirm_ingredient_substitution, get_safe_ingredient_substitutes, get_supermarket_prices, jsonb_remove_item.
  • Every project SECURITY DEFINER function resolves search_path as public, pg_temp (20261007160000); TRUNCATE, TRIGGER, REFERENCES and MAINTAIN were revoked from client roles (20261007120000).

Flow: guest onboarding

  1. Landing CTAs route to /onboarding. If there is no session, the page calls supabase.auth.signInAnonymously() and Supabase Auth returns a guest JWT with a real auth.uid() and is_anonymous = true (ADR-0003).
  2. The wizard collects diets, allergens, disliked ingredients, cuisines and household size; a draft survives reloads in session storage.
  3. The page upserts the user_profiles row under RLS (lib/api/user-profile.ts). Health data needs a health_data consent row first (trigger require_health_data_consent).
  4. It then calls menu generation (flow-menu-generation) and opens /menu.

Rules: the anonymous session is the guest's account, so logging out loses her data (the UI asks for confirmation). Abandoned guests are deleted after 3 days (automatic-processes). Anonymous sign-in is rate-limited by Supabase Auth.

Flow: weekly menu generation

  1. The browser posts {semana_iso, fecha_inicio} with its JWT to generate-meal-plan.
  2. The function authenticates the caller, applies the rate limit (5 per hour), loads user_profiles (404 without onboarding) and refuses with 409 if a plan for that week exists.
  3. get_filtered_recipes(user_id) returns the safe pool: active recipes whose alergenos do not overlap the user's, whose diet flags hold and that avoid disliked ingredients. This SQL filter is the single structural food-safety enforcement point; too small a pool answers 422, never a degraded menu.
  4. Only for Pro / Family (isProEntitlementActive): get_recent_recipe_marks (last two weeks of the user's own marks) and get_user_recipe_engagement (all-time). Free never calls them.
  5. selectMenu() (menu-selector.ts) fills each slot deterministically: time limits, no repeats within the week, variety, season of the planned week (3 points in season, 1 for todo_el_ano), history penalties, Pro engagement nudge, jitter. A Pro user's recent marks are removed from the pool, falling back to every safe candidate if that empties a meal type (ADR-0063). An empty pool gives a "no safe recipe" slot and an advertencias entry. For Pro, buildLearningExplanation() writes the "what we learned" text from a template.
  6. The function calls create_meal_plan(...) with the service role: plan and all slots in one transaction (pendiente, or excluida for meals left out of planning_selection).
  7. It returns the plan and slots with full recipes, advertencias and explicacion_aprendizaje.

Rules: allergen exclusion is a hard SQL constraint; Free structurally cannot read history; a warning is always surfaced; the plan cap (104) applies to this insert. Side effects: PostHog generation events.

Flow: shopping list

  1. The browser posts {meal_plan_id, refresh?} to generate-shopping-list (rate limit 60 per hour).
  2. Ownership is checked (404). Without refresh a list must not exist (409); with refresh it must (404).
  3. The function loads the slots' recipes, quantities (ingredientes_cantidades, else a base-quantity table), servings and any confirmed substitution.
  4. consolidateIngredientes() normalises names, scales by household size over meta.raciones and sums compatible units; classification assigns fixed walking-order aisles and a cost range. All deterministic code.
  5. It inserts the list, or in refresh mode rebuilds it in place keeping what applies, and clears desactualizada_desde.
  6. It returns the aisle-grouped list.

Later edits: tick via jsonb_set_comprado, add a favourite-based suggestion via jsonb_add_item (suggestions from get-shopping-list-suggestions, 120 per hour), undo it via jsonb_remove_item, clear bought items via jsonb_clear_comprados.

Flow: cooked and discarded marks (the learning loop)

  1. The calendar sends {meal_plan_recipe_id, estado} (and nueva_recipe_id for sustituida) to update-recipe-status (rate limit 60 per hour).
  2. The function joins the slot to its plan's owner and refuses another user's slot; a slot already cocinada or descartada is final (409). For sustituida it checks the new recipe against get_filtered_recipes and the slot's meal type. A rating in the body is ignored.
  3. It writes estado (and recipe_id on substitution) with the service role.
  4. recipe_learning_trigger fires after the update when estado changed: on the first cocinada of this user for this recipe it inserts into recipe_user_feedback, adds 1 to veces_cocinada and sets ultima_vez_en_menu; on the first descartada it adds 1 to veces_descartada. A repeat mark by the same user moves nothing. It does nothing when the session sets app.skip_recipe_learning.
  5. The function answers {ok, estado}.

Rules: recording is the same for every tier; only a Pro user's next generation reads her marks. The shopping list is marked stale when a slot becomes descartada or its recipe changes.

Flow: calendar slot swap

  1. The user drags a slot onto another of the same meal type; the browser calls swap_meal_plan_slots(p_slot_a_id, p_slot_b_id) (rate limit 120 per hour).
  2. The function (SECURITY DEFINER) checks both slots are in one plan the caller owns, share tipo_plato and are not excluida; a missing and a foreign slot get the same "not found".
  3. It exchanges recipe_id, estado and rating with learning switched off for the transaction (app.skip_recipe_learning) and app.mpr_trusted_write set.
  4. The browser keeps its optimistic swap, or reverts on error.

Why: a position change must never count as a cook or a discard (ADR-0002).

Flow: put a catalogue recipe into a slot

  1. From the recipe library the user picks an open slot; the browser calls assign_recipe_to_slot(p_slot_id, p_recipe_id) (SECURITY INVOKER).
  2. Rate limit assign_recipe_to_slot (60 per hour).
  3. RLS hides other users' slots (one error for missing and foreign). The slot must be pendiente or sustituida and its day today or later (Europe/Madrid). The recipe must pass get_filtered_recipes(auth.uid(), p_recipe_id), be active, and match the slot's tipo_plato.
  4. It sets recipe_id and clears sustitucion_ingrediente; estado is untouched, so no learning is recorded. The shopping list becomes stale.

Flow: copy a past menu ("Usar este menú")

  1. The browser calls copy_meal_plan_to_week(p_source_meal_plan_id, p_semana_iso, p_fecha_inicio) (SECURITY DEFINER, rate limit 20 per hour).
  2. The source must be the caller's (one "not found" for missing and foreign); the target must be the current or next ISO week (Madrid) and fecha_inicio its Monday.
  3. Each copied slot is re-checked against get_filtered_recipes(auth.uid()) and activo; a slot that no longer passes is written with recipe_id = null, pendiente, and the new plan carries one advertencias entry naming those slots.
  4. Any plan for the target week is replaced; every slot resets to pendiente; it returns the new plan id.

Why: an allergy declared after the source week, or a recipe re-tagged or retired since, must not come back (FRESCO-994).

Flow: delete a week's menu

deleteMealPlan() (lib/api/meal-plan.ts) deletes the meal_plans row under the owner's RLS; slots and the shopping list cascade. It is the documented way out of the generation 409 for an existing week.

Flow: per-slot ingredient substitution

  1. The slot UI asks get_safe_ingredient_substitutes(p_ingrediente) (SECURITY INVOKER, no identity parameter).
  2. It filters ingredient_substitutions against the caller's own allergens and diet and returns the candidates (fail closed).
  3. The user confirms: confirm_ingredient_substitution(p_slot_id, original, sustituto) re-checks the candidate is safe now, that the original is in the slot's recipe and that the slot is not cocinada, descartada or excluida.
  4. It stores {original, sustituto} on the slot's sustitucion_ingrediente; the recipe is never changed. The shopping list reads it and is marked stale.

Flow: guest to account conversion

  1. The guest types an email; POST /api/auth/guest-email requires a guest session, a Cloudflare Turnstile token when a site key is configured, and the guest-email-change rate limit (3 per hour).
  2. The route links the email to the guest, so Supabase Auth mails a code.
  3. The browser verifies the code with Supabase Auth and sets a password: same auth.uid(), is_anonymous becomes false, all data stays.
  4. If the email already belongs to another account, the browser signs into it on a throwaway client and sends that session token to reassign-guest-data (rate limit 5 per hour), which verifies the token (ADR-0022).
  5. It calls reassign_guest_data(from, to) with the service role: moves the guest's plans and lists, skipping weeks the target already has, re-filtering moved slots against the target's allergens, then deletes the guest.

Rules: the only cross-user write in the system; the target's profile is never merged; a conflicting week is dropped.

Flow: Pro subscription

  1. From /profile the browser calls POST /api/stripe/checkout (rate limit 10 per hour). The route requires a recorded withdrawal_waiver for the current text version and creates a hosted Checkout session (subscription, 7-day trial, client_reference_id = auth.uid()).
  2. Stripe sends events to POST /api/stripe/webhook. The route verifies the signature (per-environment secret), checks the event mode against the deploy's key, billing_mode and the profile's stripe_livemode (ADR-0061), then claims the event in stripe_webhook_events.
  3. Handled types (lib/billing/handled-events.ts): checkout.session.completed and checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded grant Pro after verifying the price; customer.subscription.updated and .deleted re-read the live subscription and write plan, expiry and payment-failure state; charge.refunded (full refund) and charge.dispute.created cancel the subscription that charge paid for, whose deletion event then downgrades.
  4. The service role writes user_profiles subscription columns and completes the claim. The grant path sends a confirmation email; a rejected send is queued in pending_confirmation_emails.
  5. POST /api/stripe/portal (20 per hour) opens the billing portal for a Pro user with a stored customer id.

Rules: only server code writes plan state; transient Stripe failures answer 500 so Stripe retries, other failures log and answer 200 (ADR-0062); cancellation takes effect at period end except refunds, disputes and account deletion. Side effects: server-side PostHog funnel events, gated on analytics_consent.

Flow: daily Stripe reconciliation

  1. pg_cron job stripe-reconcile-subscriptions (04:17 UTC) calls GET https://fresco-pro.vercel.app/api/cron/stripe-reconcile through pg_net with a bearer secret from Supabase Vault (fire and forget).
  2. The route checks the secret, then loads every profile with a stripe_subscription_id.
  3. For each it retrieves the subscription from Stripe and computes the target state with the webhook's own resolvers.
  4. It writes only drifted columns, downgrades paid plans that have no subscription, grants Pro for paid checkouts of the last 48 hours that never reached the profile, and retries queued confirmation emails.
  5. After a full pass it upserts job_heartbeat('stripe-reconcile').

Why: a lost webhook would otherwise leave the profile wrong forever (ADR-0015).

Flow: account deletion

  1. From the danger zone the browser calls delete-account with a recent re-authentication token (ADR-0023, rate limit 5 per hour).
  2. If a Stripe customer exists, the function cancels billing immediately with a prorated refund; if Stripe is unreachable it answers 502 and deletes nothing (ADR-0043).
  3. It deletes the auth.users row; ON DELETE CASCADE removes every owned row.
  4. It asks PostHog to delete the person; a failure does not block the deletion.
  5. It inserts an account_erasures row (hash, Stripe and PostHog outcome). A failed PostHog erasure is retried daily by retry-posthog-erasures (up to 10 attempts).

Rule: a billing failure holds the deletion back; an analytics failure does not.

Flow: weekly re-engagement push

  1. pg_cron job send-weekly-reengagement-push (Sunday 18:00 UTC) posts to the Edge Function through pg_net with a Vault-held key.
  2. The function reads get_push_subscriptions_without_current_plan(current week): subscriptions of users with no plan this week.
  3. It sends one VAPID-signed Web Push per subscription (web-push library).
  4. It prunes rows whose push service answers 404 or 410, updates last_used_at on success and writes its heartbeat.

Flow: recording consents

  1. The browser posts {kinds} to /api/consents.
  2. The route takes the user from the verified session (guests included) and the text version from LEGAL_TEXTS_VERSION.
  3. It calls record_consents with the service role; repeats are no-ops except the per-purchase withdrawal waiver.

Downstream: health data on the profile is refused without a health_data row; checkout requires a current withdrawal_waiver; the cookie-banner choice is mirrored to user_profiles.analytics_consent by components/auth/analytics-consent-sync.tsx.

Flow: launch waitlist (double opt-in)

  1. A visitor posts an email and a consent tick to /api/waitlist; the route limits per client address (check_ip_rate_limit, hashed address in ip_rate_limits).
  2. It calls request_waitlist_signup(email, version, token_hash) with the service role: an unconfirmed row with the hash of a random token.
  3. It emails the token (sendWaitlistConfirmationEmail).
  4. The visitor opens the link; /api/waitlist/confirm calls confirm_waitlist_signup(token_hash), which sets confirmed_at. The same token removes the row (remove_waitlist_signup).

Rules: nobody is mailed unless confirmed; retention 7 days unconfirmed, 12 months confirmed (job purge-waitlist-signups).

Flow: writing the recipe catalogue

  1. The owner writes recipes with the service role (offline scripts or data migrations); no client can.
  2. On an active row, recipes_tag_coherence checks allergen and diet tags against the ingredients and steps.
  3. recipes_temporada_coherence checks the season against compute_recipe_season.
  4. The row is stored, or the write fails with SQLSTATE 23514 naming each broken rule. Inactive drafts skip the ingredient-dependent checks.

Also: /admin/recipes hard-deletes a recipe through delete-catalog-recipe, gated by an ADMIN_USER_ID allowlist and refused (409) while a slot references it. supabase/seed.sql is regenerated from production (2026-10-29: 1287 rows). A nightly GitHub workflow audits the hosted catalogue's tags (hosted-catalog-allergen-audit.yml, 04:41 UTC).

Flow: supermarket price refresh

  1. A manually dispatched workflow runs scripts/refresh-supermarket-prices.ts --apply (no schedule on purpose: it writes the shared database).
  2. The script reads demand with get_supermarket_demand and checks the legal gate twice: habilitada in the database and a runnable connector in code.
  3. It fetches prices from the source (Mercadona through a community dataset, ADR-0028).
  4. It upserts supermarket_price and appends history only on change; undatable or non-positive prices are never written.

Users read through get_supermarket_prices(ingredientes, zona) (max 200 keys, fail closed on the gate).

Flow: notices centre

/notifications reads user_profiles flags and the safe catalogue and shows, in order: a payment-failed notice (Pro with payment_failed_at), a one-time welcome card, a dismissable routes guide and up to three recommended recipes. Dismissals persist in aviso_bienvenida_visto / aviso_rutas_descartado. Passive content only, no push or email. Carried from the legacy map; not re-traced in code this pass.

Flow: profile export

GET /api/profile/export ("Backup CSV") reads every table the caller owns with her own session (no service role, so RLS bounds it) and returns one multi-section CSV. Rate limit profile-export, 10 per hour.

Integration: Stripe

What it does: the whole Pro subscription: hosted Checkout, Billing Portal, webhook events, daily reconciliation and, from delete-account only, immediate cancellation with refund (stripe package, package.json).

Entities changed: user_profiles subscription columns and stripe_livemode, stripe_webhook_events, pending_confirmation_emails; read: billing_mode, user_consents (withdrawal waiver).

Dependent flows: flow-pro-subscription, flow-stripe-reconciliation, flow-account-deletion, flow-menu-generation (reads plan), flow-notices-center.

Failure behaviour: checkout or portal failure returns an error and writes nothing; a bad signature answers 400; a transient Stripe failure inside the webhook answers 500 so Stripe retries, other handler failures log and answer 200; a lost webhook is corrected by the next daily reconciliation; account deletion refuses to proceed if billing cannot be cancelled. A wrong-mode event is refused.

Integration: PostHog

What it does: product analytics in the browser (posthog-js) and from the server and Edge Functions (posthog-node, _shared/posthog.ts): generation, marks, signup and Stripe funnel events.

Entities changed: none in the app database by analytics itself. Server events are sent only when user_profiles.analytics_consent is exactly true. Erasure outcomes are recorded in account_erasures.

Dependent flows: flow-account-deletion and the guest cleanup (person erasure), flow-consents.

Failure behaviour: captures fail silently; an erasure failure is retried daily up to 10 times.

Integration: Sentry

What it does: error tracking in the Next.js runtimes (@sentry/nextjs) and from Edge Functions on unexpected 500s; the browser SDK starts only after cookie consent (ADR-0065). Entities changed: none. Failure behaviour: observability degrades; the app is unaffected.

Integration: email (Gmail SMTP and Resend)

What it does: sends the subscription confirmation and the waitlist confirmation token. When GMAIL_SMTP_APP_PASSWORD is configured the app sends through the Gmail account Supabase Auth already uses (nodemailer, lib/email/gmail-smtp.ts); otherwise through Resend from onboarding@resend.dev, which only reaches the account owner while there is no verified domain. Auth codes (signup, guest conversion) are sent by Supabase Auth, not by this code.

Entities changed: pending_confirmation_emails (a rejected subscription confirmation is queued and retried by the reconcile job).

Dependent flows: flow-pro-subscription, flow-stripe-reconciliation, flow-waitlist.

Failure behaviour: a subscription confirmation that fails is retried daily under a cap; the subscription itself is unaffected.

Integration: Web Push services

What it does: delivers the weekly reminder to browser push services; endpoints must be https on an allow-listed host (FCM, Mozilla, Apple, Windows). Entities changed: push_subscriptions (rows deleted on 404 / 410, last_used_at on success). Dependent flows: flow-weekly-push. Failure behaviour: per subscription; one bad send never aborts the batch.

Integration: Supabase Auth

What it does: the only identity provider: email and password, anonymous guests, email-change codes, recovery and admin deletion. Entities changed: auth.users, the cascade root of all user data; is_anonymous drives guest cleanup and reassignment. Failure behaviour: anonymous sign-in and email sending are rate-limited by Supabase; the sender is a Gmail account with a daily cap (ADR-0021).

Integration: Cloudflare (Turnstile and R2)

Turnstile protects POST /api/auth/guest-email: with a site key in the build a valid token is required (400 when missing or rejected, 503 when the secret is missing or Cloudflare does not answer). R2 stores the encrypted daily database backup made by db-backup.yml (carried from the legacy map, not re-read). Neither writes application data.
